subject: Staged onboarding: Nyx-7B-slim variant — compatibility sweep and temporary version hold
messages:
From: Nyx Onboarding <onboarding@nyxai.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: platform-eng@nyxai.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: NYX-7B-slim - intake + compatibility artifacts (requesting short-term pin)

Hi Hannah / Redwood team,

Thanks again for early intake on the Nyx side. We're sharing the initial artifacts for the "nyx-7b-slim" variant we're planning to ship for low-latency workloads. Primary asks: 1) quick compatibility sweep for tokenizer/kv behavior, 2) telemetry hooks to validate prompt-level regressions, and 3) a short-term version pin during the staged onboarding window so we can iterate without traffic variance.

Attached: nyx_slim_weights_manifest.csv (weights manifest), telemetry_matrix.xlsx (suggested metrics), and a short compatibility summary. Our target timeline is a two-week staged rollout starting July 3 — we understand Redwood's checks may push that out.

Notes: the slim variant uses a fused rotary implementation that differs slightly in key cache layout; we included a short compatibility shim in the manifest (flag: use_rotary_compat=true). We'd like to request a temporary model-version hold (pin) to nyx-7b-slim-v2 while the compatibility sweep and telemetry collection complete.

Would appreciate confirmation on the earliest you can run the compatibility pass and whether an operator pin is the correct interim control.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Onboarding Lead, Nyx AI
Attachment: nyx_slim_weights_manifest.csv (CSV, 14KB)
Attachment: telemetry_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nyx Onboarding <onboarding@nyxai.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NYX-7B-slim - intake + compatibility artifacts (requesting short-term pin)

Thanks Asha — quick read through looks reasonable. A few immediate asks from our side so we can scope the work:

- Prio: compatibility sweep (tokenizer + KV cache behavior) and a smoke generation regression over our standard prompt set (10K tokens, multi-turn).
- Telemetry: we need explicit names for any custom fields (e.g., "nyx_rotary_mode") you want surfaced via our per-request trace span; please add to the telemetry spreadsheet.
- Pin: operator-side temporary pin to nyx-7b-slim-v2 is fine for the staging window, but we require an explicit rollback/fallback variant to be configured (fallback: nyx-7b-std).

@Priyom — can you own the compatibility sweep? If it returns any KV layout mismatches we may need a short compatibility shim in the runtime. @Marissa — please book a quick 30-min canary sync for tomorrow to align telemetry and canary thresholds.

Asha — can you confirm you can hold traffic for 48 hrs at the end of the staged run for us to validate metrics?

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: onboarding@nyxai.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NYX-7B-slim - intake + compatibility artifacts (requesting short-term pin)

On Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 11:03 AM hannah_schmitt@redwood.com wrote:
> @Priyom — can you own the compatibility sweep? If it returns any KV layout mismatches we may need a short compatibility shim in the runtime.

I'll take this. Initial dev notes after a local smoke:

- Tokenizer: models use a small byte-level tweak; detokenization is fine but the tokenizer mapping table requires a patch to our BPE loader. Patch is low-risk (mapping diff + test cases).
- KV cache: layout differs in the low-level ordering for rotary kv pairs. We can add a compatibility shim to the KV serializer that rearranges the pairs for older runtime versions; this adds ~0.6ms per request at 1K tokens on an A100 (acceptable for staging).
- Telemetry: I added a recommended span name (nyx.variant.flags) to the shared telemetry sheet and listed the minimal fields we need: variant_id, rotary_mode, quant_profile.

Pin request: I support a short-term operator pin to nyx-7b-slim-v2 for the staging window. If we see any unexpected regression in the first 24 hrs we should auto-fallback to nyx-7b-std and open a rapid incident. I uploaded a small excerpt of the compatibility run (compatibility_check_excerpt.log).

Next steps:
1) Marissa to schedule the canary sync (30m).
2) Hannah to approve the operator pin and the fallback override.
3) I will validate the shim in staging and report perf delta by EOD July 2.

—Priyom
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachment: compatibility_check_excerpt.log (TXT, 8KB)

From: Nyx Onboarding <onboarding@nyxai.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: platform-eng@nyxai.com, ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NYX-7B-slim - intake + compatibility artifacts (requesting short-term pin)

Thanks team — this aligns with our expectations. We can hold traffic for the 48-hr quiet window at the end of your staged run (targeting July 10–11) and will enable a hotfix branch with the compatibility shim if Redwood prefers to avoid a runtime change.

We're okay with a temporary operator pin to nyx-7b-slim-v2 for the staging window. Please confirm the exact pin command or management link and the fallback policy (we prefer automated fallback to nyx-7b-std after two failed health checks).

Also attaching a short doc that maps our internal rotary_mode flags to the telemetry fields you requested; uploaded to the Drive link in the thread.

—Asha Rao
Onboarding Lead, Nyx AI
Attachment: telemetry_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)
